entry: 2007 first-person shooter video game. Developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision, it is the fourth main installment in the [[Call of Duty|Call of Duty series]] and breaks away from the [[World War II]] setting of earlier entries to a modern military setting. Released in November 2007 for [[PlayStation 3]], [[Xbox 360]] and [[Microsoft Windows]], it was critically acclaimed and was the top-selling game worldwide in 2007, selling around seven million copies by January 2008.

First-person shooter video game series and media franchise, published by Activision from 2003. Developed first by Infinity Ward and later by Treyarch, Sledgehammer Games and Raven Software, the series originally focused on [[World War II]] settings. [[Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare]] (2007), which introduced a modern setting, became its breakthrough. As of October 2023 it had sold over 500 million copies and generated $30 billion in revenue by 2022. [[Guinness World Records]] has verified it as the best-selling first-person shooter series.

Family of [[Fly|flies]] in the order Diptera, commonly called blowflies or carrion flies. Adults are often shiny, with blue, green or black thoraces and abdomens. Most [[Larva|larvae]] are scavengers of carrion and dung; the maggots, known as gentles, are often used as fishing bait. A female typically lays 150–200 eggs per batch, and the larvae use enzymes to break down the proteins they feed on. Their predictable development on corpses aids in estimating postmortem intervals. Adults are occasional pollinators, attracted to flowers with [[Odor|odors]] resembling rotting meat. Some species, such as *Chrysomya bezziana*, cause myiasis, while *Lucilia sericata* is used in maggot debridement therapy for wound healing. Its monophyly is disputed: some studies describe the family as polyphyletic, while recent phylogenomic analyses support monophyly.

Second-largest moon of [[Jupiter]], after [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]], and the third-largest in the [[Solar System]]. At 4,821 km in diameter, it is nearly as large as the planet [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], though with only about a third of that planet's mass. It is the outermost of Jupiter's four large Galilean moons, discovered in 1610 by Simon Marius and [[Galileo Galilei]]. Its surface is the oldest and most heavily cratered in the Solar System, with no sign of plate tectonics or volcanism. Composed of roughly equal parts rock and ice, Callisto has a density of about 1.83 g/cm³, the lowest of Jupiter's major moons. Investigation by the Galileo spacecraft suggested a small silicate core and possibly a subsurface ocean of liquid water.

Unit of [[Energy|energy]] used in nutrition and food science, originating in the caloric theory of heat. The small calorie is the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius. The large calorie, or kilocalorie, equals 1,000 small calories and is normally the unit used for the energy values of foods; some authors write Calorie with a capital C for it. The calorie is not part of the [[International System of Units|SI]] and is regarded as obsolete, having been replaced by the [[Joule|joule]]. The thermochemical calorie is now taken as exactly 4.184 J, so one kilocalorie is 4184 J, or 4.184 kJ.

30th [[President of the United States|president of the United States]] (1923–29). A [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] lawyer from [[Massachusetts]], he was governor of that state from 1919 to 1921 and vice president under Warren G. Harding until Harding's death in 1923. Known as "Silent Cal" for his taciturn manner, he signed the Indian Citizenship Act of 1924, which granted U.S. citizenship to all Native Americans. Advocates of smaller government praise his hands-off, pro-business approach, while critics argue that he failed to use the economic boom of the [[Roaring Twenties]] to help struggling farmers and workers.

Scottish DJ, record producer, singer and songwriter, known professionally as Calvin Harris (real name Adam Richard Wiles). His album *18 Months* (2012) topped the UK Albums Chart, and in 2013 he surpassed the record of [[Michael Jackson]] for most top ten singles from one album, with nine from *18 Months* against Jackson's seven. He was the first UK solo artist to reach more than one billion streams on [[Spotify]]. He won British Producer of the Year and British Single of the Year at the 2019 Brit Awards, and topped [[Forbes]]' list of the world's highest-paid DJs for six consecutive years, from 2013 to 2018.

American [[Fashion design|fashion]] designer. In 1968 he launched, with childhood friend Barry K. Schwartz, the company that later became Calvin Klein. He was hailed as the new [[Yves Saint Laurent (designer)|Yves Saint Laurent]] for his clean lines, and his tight-fitting signature jeans of 1974 went on to gross $200,000 in their first week of sales. His name also appears on a range of [[Perfume|perfumes]], [[Watch|watches]] and [[Jewellery|jewelry]]. In 2003 he sold his majority stake in the company to Phillips-Van Heusen Corporation for $430 million.

Country in Southeast Asia, officially the Kingdom of Cambodia, with a population of about 17.6 million as of 2024, predominantly ethnic Khmer. Its capital and largest city is [[Phnom Penh]]. The [[Khmer Empire]] (9th to 15th centuries) built [[Angkor Wat]], and Cambodia was a French protectorate from 1863 until independence in 1953. The [[Khmer Rouge]] regime carried out the [[Cambodian genocide]] from 1975 to 1979, and a later Vietnamese invasion ousted it. UN-supervised elections in 1993 restored a [[Constitutional monarchy|constitutional monarchy]]. The Cambodian People's Party has dominated politics, and agriculture remains the largest economic sector, with growth in garments, tourism and construction.

Armed conflict (1978–89) between Democratic Kampuchea and [[Vietnam]]. Vietnamese forces launched a full-scale invasion on December 25, 1978, toppling the [[Khmer Rouge]] regime and occupying Cambodia. Vietnam was backed by the [[Soviet Union]], while the Khmer Rouge had the support of [[China]]. Khmer Rouge remnants and other factions fought the occupation until Vietnam withdrew its troops in September 1989. The Paris Peace Agreements of 1991 led to a UN-led transition and the restoration of a constitutional monarchy in 1993.

Systematic persecution and killing of Cambodian citizens by the [[Khmer Rouge]] regime, 1975–79. Led by [[Pol Pot]], the Communist Party of Kampuchea emptied the cities and forced people into labor camps, where mass executions, forced labor, starvation and disease were rampant. Approximately 1.5 to 2 million people died, or 20% to 25% of the 1975 population, including ethnic minorities such as the Cham. China supplied at least 90% of the Khmer Rouge's foreign aid, and the [[Chinese Communist Party]] led by [[Mao Zedong]] supported the movement. A Vietnamese invasion toppled the regime in 1978. In 2019 the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia found Nuon Chea and Khieu Samphan guilty of crimes against humanity and genocide, and both were sentenced to life imprisonment.

First geological period of the [[Paleozoic]] Era and the [[Phanerozoic]] Eon. It lasted 51.95 million years, from 538.8 to 486.85 million years ago, following the [[Ediacaran|Ediacaran Period]] and preceding the [[Ordovician]]. Most continents lay in the Southern Hemisphere, and the assembly of [[Gondwana]] helped drive up global temperatures. The period saw the [[Cambrian explosion]], a rapid increase in fossil diversity that produced the first representatives of most modern animal phyla. No land animals or plants had yet evolved, and [[Trilobite|trilobites]] were among the prominent animals. The Cambrian also has an unusually high proportion of lagerstätte deposits, sites where soft body parts are exceptionally preserved.

Major evolutionary radiation of [[Animal|animal]] life beginning about 538.8 million years ago in the early [[Cambrian]] period. Fossils from the period include representatives of all five modern animal phyla except [[Sponge|sponges]], which appeared earlier. Many Cambrian animals were more mobile and had more complex body plans than the [[Ediacaran|Ediacaran biota]] that preceded them. The radiation lasted between 13 million and 25 million years, ending at the Sinsk Event, and resulted in the divergence of most extant eumetazoan phyla. It coincided with the evolution of mineralized skeletons, which fossilize readily and contributed to the abundance of early Cambrian [[Fossil|fossils]]. Proposed causes include a rise in oxygen levels and ecological factors such as [[Predation|predation]].

City (pop., 2021: 145,700), county town of Cambridgeshire, England, on the River Cam, 55 miles (89 km) north of [[London]]. It is home to the [[University of Cambridge]], founded in 1209, whose buildings include King's College Chapel and the Cavendish Laboratory. The city is at the heart of the Silicon Fen high-technology cluster, where software and bioscience firms have grown out of the university. Over 40 percent of its workforce holds a higher education qualification. The city produced the first Laws of the Game for [[Association football|association football]].

City (pop., 2020: 118,403) in Middlesex County, Massachusetts, across the Charles River from [[Boston]]. It was named for the [[University of Cambridge]] in England and founded in December 1630. Cambridge Common, celebrated as the birthplace of the Continental Army, is where [[George Washington]] took command of the Patriot soldiers in July 1775. [[Harvard University]], founded in 1636, is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States. The [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) has a 168-acre campus here, and in 2022 the city was home to over 250 biotech companies.

Even-toed ungulate in the genus *Camelus*, with fatty humps on its back, long domesticated for transport, milk, meat and fiber. There are three surviving species: the one-humped [[Dromedary]] and the two-humped [[Bactrian camel]], as well as the wild Bactrian camel, a distinct species that is endangered with around 1,000 individuals. Camels are adapted to desert habitats and are vital working animals that carry passengers and cargo. The wider family Camelidae includes the [[Llama|llama]], [[Alpaca|alpaca]], guanaco and vicuña. Camelids originated in North America during the [[Eocene]]; the ancestor of modern camels crossed into Asia during the late [[Miocene]], about 6 million years ago.

Genus of flowering plants in the tea family, Theaceae, native to tropical and subtropical areas of eastern and southern Asia. It has more than 220 described species, almost all found in southern China and Indochina. Camellias have been cultivated for centuries as ornamental, tea and oil plants, and over 26,000 [[Cultivar|cultivars]] have been registered. The leaves of [[Camellia sinensis|*C. sinensis*]] are processed into [[Tea|tea]], which is of particular economic importance in East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent. The ornamental *C. japonica* and *C. sasanqua* and their hybrids are the source of hundreds of garden cultivars, and *C. oleifera* produces tea seed oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

Evergreen [[Shrub|shrub]] in the family Theaceae, also called the tea plant. Its leaves, buds and stems are harvested to make [[Tea|tea]]; the leaves are processed to different degrees of oxidation to produce white, yellow, green, oolong, dark and black teas. The species is native to the highlands between southwestern China, northern Myanmar and northeastern India, and is now cultivated as a cash crop in many other parts of the world. China, India and Kenya are the three largest tea-producing countries.

Darkened chamber or box that projects an inverted, reversed image of the outside view through a small hole or [[Lens|lens]]. Versions with lenses, used since the second half of the 16th century, became popular drawing aids because they gave accurate [[Perspective (graphical)|perspective]]. The device was also used to study [[Solar eclipse|solar eclipses]] without looking directly at the Sun. In the first half of the 19th century it was developed into the [[Camera|photographic camera]], with light-sensitive materials exposed to the projected image. The term was first used in 1604.

American actress and author. Her films have grossed over $3 billion at the U.S. box office, and her romantic comedies of the late 1990s and early 2000s, including *There's Something About Mary* (1998), made her a prominent [[Sex symbol|sex symbol]]. She has voiced Princess Fiona in the [[Shrek]] franchise since 2001. After retiring from acting in 2014 to focus on family, she returned with *Back in Action* (2025). Her health book *The Body Book* (2013) was a *New York Times* bestseller. In 2015 she married the Good Charlotte guitarist Benji Madden, and the couple have had children through surrogacy.

Country in [[Central Africa]] (pop., 2024: 30.97 million), officially the Republic of Cameroon. Its capital is [[Yaoundé]], and its coastline lies on the [[Gulf of Guinea]]. Its population speaks 250 native languages, and English and French are official languages. Portuguese explorers reached the coast in the 15th century. Cameroon gained independence from [[France]] on January 1, 1960. [[Paul Biya]] has held power since November 6, 1982; critics argue that elections have been manipulated and political opposition suppressed.

Danish-French Impressionist and Neo-Impressionist painter, born on Saint Thomas in the Danish West Indies, now the [[United States Virgin Islands]]. He is the only artist to have exhibited at all eight [[Impressionism|Impressionist]] exhibitions in Paris, held from 1874 to 1886. In 1873 he helped found a collective of 15 artists. Art historian John Rewald called him the "dean of the Impressionist painters". At the age of 54 he took up Neo-Impressionism, working with [[Georges Seurat]]. He acted as a father figure to [[Paul Cézanne|Cézanne]], Seurat, [[Paul Gauguin|Gauguin]] and Van Gogh.

Italian statesman and leader of the movement for Italian unification. He was Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia from 1852 until his death, apart from a six-month resignation, and the first Prime Minister of the [[Kingdom of Italy]] in 1861. As prime minister he steered [[Piedmont]] through the [[Crimean War]] and the Second Italian War of Independence, and backed the campaigns of [[Giuseppe Garibaldi]], maneuvering Piedmont into a new great power and controlling a nearly united Italy five times as large as Piedmont had been before he came to power. He pushed economic reforms in Piedmont and founded the newspaper *Il Risorgimento*. Historian Denis Mack Smith called him the most successful parliamentarian in Italian history but not especially democratic, saying he was often dictatorial and interfered in parliamentary elections.

Network of pilgrim routes leading to the shrine of the apostle James in the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, in [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]], northwestern Spain. Established in the early 9th century after the discovery of the relics of Saint James, it became a major medieval [[Pilgrimage|pilgrimage]] route from the 10th century. After the Granada War ended in 1492, [[Pope Alexander VI]] declared it one of the "three great pilgrimages of Christendom". The Council of Europe named it the first Cultural Route in 1987. Its French Way and northern routes in Spain are on the [[UNESCO]] World Heritage List.

Concealment of animals or objects by coloration, pattern, materials or illumination, either by making them hard to see or by disguising them as something else. Most camouflage aims at crypsis, through background matching, disruptive coloration and countershading. A third approach, motion dazzle, uses a conspicuous pattern to make an object momentarily harder to locate. Some animals, such as [[Chameleon|chameleons]] and [[Octopus|octopuses]], can actively change their skin patterns and colors, while [[Cephalopod|cephalopods]] such as [[Squid|squid]] use light for counter-illumination. Military camouflage developed rapidly during [[World War I]], when merchant ships were painted in dazzle patterns to confuse enemy submarines about a target's speed and heading. Since the mid-20th century, [[Radar|radar]] has largely made camouflage obsolete for fixed-wing military aircraft. Camouflage patterns are also widely used in [[Fashion|fashion]] clothing.
